subject: Commercialization rights & feedback license — evidence request
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@nimbushealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Lee <jlee@nimbushealth.com>, procure@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercialization rights & feedback license — initial redlines

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are our legal redlines to the MSA and Order Form (Nimbus_Redlines_v2.docx). Two main asks we want to make explicit:

- No downstream productization: we cannot consent to Redwood or third parties using our customer outputs to create derivative products that compete with Nimbus.
- Training prohibition: we require explicit opt-in before any of our data/outputs are used to train Redwood models.

We are otherwise open to a limited, non-exclusive feedback license for telemetry and quality monitoring provided it is aggregated and non-identifiable.

Can you confirm what evidence you can share about:
1) How Customer outputs are stored and segregated on your hosted environment;
2) Whether Redwood performs any offline tuning on models that could incorporate customer data; and
3) Your suggested language to preserve our productization carveouts while allowing Redwood to operate.

We need this resolved for the procurement review next week.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Product Partnerships
Nimbus Health

--
Attachment: Nimbus_Redlines_v2.docx (docx, 124KB)

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercialization rights & feedback license — initial redlines

Hi Sofia —

Appreciate the clarity and the quick turnaround on the redlines. Short answers up-front:

- Storage/segregation: customer data and derived outputs for hosted customers are logically segregated by tenant; we have role-based access controls and encryption at rest. I can share a short evidence matrix that maps controls to the items procurement cares about.
- Offline tuning: Redwood does not use customer data for model training without explicit opt-in. We should make that language explicit and machine-actionable in the Order Form.
- Productization carveouts: we hear you on downstream productization — we have a proposed compromise that allows aggregated feedback for quality improvements but excludes commercialization of Customer-specific output.

I'm looping in Laura and Ben from legal to propose precise language. We will also attach an evidence matrix for your procurement and security teams.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to propose redline language by EOD today.
2) Ben to prepare evidence_matrix.xlsx covering encryption, access, and training practices.
3) Both parties to review and aim to finalize a narrow amendment to the MSA/Order Form by Thursday.

Would Thursday afternoon work for a short wrap-up call?

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: evidence_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28KB)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Commercialization rights & feedback license — initial redlines

Folks —

Draft guidance below for a narrow amendment (will put in doc form):

- Training: add explicit clause in Order Form: "Customer Data and Customer Outputs will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any production or research model without Customer's prior written opt-in."

- Productization: add an Order Form carveout: "Customer retains all rights to Customer Outputs. Redwood will not commercialize, sell, license, or otherwise distribute Customer Outputs or derivatives thereof as a product or service designed to compete with Customer without Customer's express written consent."

- Feedback/Telemetry: allow a limited, non-exclusive, revocable feedback license for aggregated, de-identified telemetry for the sole purpose of model and service improvement; include an audit right for an independent third party once annually.

- Evidence: propose to produce the evidence_matrix.xlsx plus a short attestation letter from our InfoSec lead about segregation and encryption.

Open questions: 1) Is the annual third-party audit acceptable to Nimbus? 2) For opt-in language, do they want a per-model toggle or an account-level election?

I'll draft the amendment and redline the Nimbus doc. Ben, please populate the evidence sheet and include retention and deletion timelines.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_proposed_amendment.docx (docx, 36KB)

From: Jared Lee <jlee@nimbushealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@nimbushealth.com>, procure@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-06-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercialization rights & feedback license — Nimbus response

Laura / Priyom —

Thanks for the quick reply and the draft language. A few points from our side:

- Annual third-party audit is reasonable but we need scope to include model retraining logs and access controls.
- Opt-in granularity: product team prefers account-level opt-in for simplicity; legal would like a per-model checkbox where feasible. We can accept account-level if the opt-in process is auditable and reversible.
- Evidence: the procurement team needs retention and deletion timelines for Customer Outputs; please include a 90-day purge option for non-production test artifacts unless otherwise agreed.

If you can incorporate these items into the amendment and send redlines, we'll route to procurement and aim for signature before week end.

Regards,
Jared Lee
General Counsel
Nimbus Health

--
Attachment: —

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@nimbushealth.com>, Jared Lee <jlee@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercialization rights & feedback license — proposal & next steps

Sofia/Jared —

Thanks — attached is our proposed amendment (redwood_proposed_amendment.docx) plus the evidence_matrix.xlsx Ben prepared. Highlights:

- Training: explicit opt-in clause; account-level toggle with audit logs and an exportable consent record.
- Productization: explicit carveout preventing Redwood from packaging Customer Outputs into standalone competing products; allows aggregated, de-identified signal for model health.
- Audit: we accept an annual third-party review limited to controls related to segregation, retention, and retraining logs (scoped and redacted for proprietary infra details).
- Retention: default retention for Customer Outputs is 365 days; we offer a 90-day purge option (as requested) for non-prod/test artifacts with a contract note.

Next steps:
1) Please review attached redlines and evidence sheet.
2) If acceptable, confirm procurement will proceed to signature and we will route the amendment to DocuSign (link attached).
3) If you want a quick 20-minute call tomorrow to finalize language, happy to schedule.

Appreciate the collaboration — our goal is to preserve Nimbus's product rights while keeping the path for Redwood to operate and improve service quality.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_proposed_amendment.docx (docx, 36KB); evidence_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28KB)
